summary: Anagarika Dharmapala was a Buddhist studies and religious studies figure who studied at S. Thomas' College (~1876-1883), Sri Jayawardenepura Maha Vidyalaya, St. Benedict's College, and Royal College, Colombo. He founded the Maha Bodhi Society in 1891 and the Maha Bodhi Society of India.

Anagarika Govinda worked in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and philosophy, earning a doctorate at the University of Freiburg and studying under Nyanatiloka Mahathera and Tomo Geshe Rinpoche. He taught at Visva-Bharati (1931-1935) and Patna University (1935-1936), and served as Ācārya of Arya Maitreya Mandala (~1933-1985).

Anagarika Munindra was a Buddhist and religious studies teacher who studied under Satya Narayan Goenka and disciple of Mahasi Sayadaw (1957-1966). He served as superintendent at the Mahabodhi Temple from 1953 to 1957.

Anam Thubten Rinpoche is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar who studied under traditional teacher Tsurlo Rinpoche. He served as a teacher at the Vajrayana Foundation College of Buddhist Studies.

Ananda Guruge was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who earned degrees from the University of Ceylon (-1947) and the University of London. He was Professor of Educational Planning at NIEPA (attested 1970) and Dean Emeritus of Academic Affairs at University of the West (attested 2012).

Ananda K. Coomaraswamy was an Indology, history, and philosophy scholar who studied at University College London and under Caroline Rhys Davids. He directed the Geological Survey of Ceylon (~1903-1906) and served as curator and research fellow at the Museum of Fine Arts, Boston (1917, 1933).

Anant Sadashiv Altekar was an Indology and history/archaeology scholar. He held professorships at Banaras Hindu University (~1930-1949) and Patna University (~1949-1957), chaired the Numismatic Society of India (1947), and served as Director of the K. P. Jayaswal Research Institute (~1954-1959).

Anantalal Thakur was a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He served as a professor at the Mithila Sanskrit Research Institute (~1955-1974) and as Director of the K. P. Jayaswal Research Institute (1968-1971).

Anantanand Rambachan is a religious studies, philosophy, and Indology scholar. He studied at the University of the West Indies, under Swami Dayananda Saraswati (~1976-1979), and at the University of Leeds (~1981-1984), later serving as professor of religion at St. Olaf College (~1985-2021).

Andrea Acri is an Indology and religious studies scholar. He completed his PhD at Leiden University (~2006-2011) supervised by Arlo Griffiths and Willem van der Molen, and was appointed maître de conférences/assistant professor in tantric studies at the EPHE in 2016.

Andrea R. Jain is a religious studies and Indology scholar who earned her PhD from Rice University (2004-2010). She joined Indiana University in 2010, rising to associate professor (2016) and full professor (2021).
Andrea Schlosser is a scholar in Indology and Buddhist studies who completed both a master's degree (by 2008) and a PhD (by 2014) at the Free University of Berlin.

Andreas Doctor is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who completed his PhD at the University of Calgary under doctoral supervisor Leslie S. Kawamura. He also studied under traditional teachers Chokyi Nyima Rinpoche, Tsikey Chokling Rinpoche, and Phakchok Rinpoche.
Andreas Spengel was a linguistics scholar who studied at the University of Munich (~1856-1860) and the Frederick William University Berlin (~1860-1862). He later taught Albert Grünwedel.

Andree Dominique Messent is a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar who earned a PhD at the University of Bristol under the supervision of Paul Williams, having also studied under Rupert Gethin and Ulrich Pagel.
Andrew B. Irvine is a scholar of philosophy and religious studies who earned a PhD from Boston University. He held an attested post as Assistant Professor of Philosophy at Maryville College in 2009.
Andrew Garrett is a linguistics scholar who studied at Harvard University (~1983-1990). He has held a post at the University of California, Berkeley since approximately 1995.

Andrew Glass is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and linguistics. He completed an MA (-2000) and PhD (-2006) at the University of Washington under Richard Salomon, and also studied at Bukkyo University (2003).
Andrew Goudie is an archaeology and history scholar who studied at Dean Close School and Trinity Hall, Cambridge (~1964-1970). He served as a professor at the University of Oxford from 1970 to 2014.
Andrew J. Nicholson is an Indology and philosophy scholar who studied under traditional teacher Shrinarayan Mishra. He holds a post at Stony Brook University.
